content_list.content_text: Between the release of The Wild One (1953) and Easy Rider (1969), Hollywood entered into a long and troubled relationship with American youth, explaining, indulging and exploiting the phenomenon of adolescence. Although important in their day, these teen-oriented films are by definition ephemeral, and only a few managed to make the theme of the mid-twentieth-century generation gap endure.

information.contentText: This film is famous for pioneering the depiction of motorcycle gangs, which would later appear in films such as The Wild Angels (1966) and Easy Rider (1969). Brando and his leather jacket would become a cultural icon of the 1950s.

content_list.content_text: The Wild One, directed by László Benedek (1905-1992), is generally considered the starting point of this phase, although it is only tangentially aimed at a teenage audience; the film's bikers seem more like outlaw cowboys than rebellious teenagers. Marlon Brando (1924-2004) was almost 30 when he made the film, but his inarticulate grace, along with his sunglasses, his leather jacket and his air of vague superiority, made him, for a brief time, the symbol of disaffected youth.

content_list.title: Biker Movies
content_list.description: Several productions followed The Wild One in the 1990s, among them Motorcycle Gang (1957) and the underground film Scorpio Rising (1964), directed by Kenneth Anger (b. 1927). But biker movies only emerged as a subgenre after the success of Roger Corman's The Wild Angels (1966). Variations featured female gangs in The Mini-Skirt Mob (1968) and bikers in The Losers (1970); there was also the self-explanatory Werewolves on Wheels (1971). The Wild Angels also inspired Easy Rider (1969), a more artistic film that gave rise to the road movies of the 1970s, including Electra Glide in Blue (1973). Biker films remain nostalgic; the formula also gave rise to the TV series Sons of Anarchy (2008-2014).

content_list.content_text: James Dean (1931-1955) replaced Brando's intermittent intensity with an introspective hurt. In his first major film, East of Eden (1955), directed by Elia Kazan (1909-2003), Dean's portrayal of an unstable son fighting for his father's love hit young audiences of the mid-1950s hard. Released the same year, the urban drama Rebel Without a Cause (1955), directed by Nicholas Ray (1911-1979), took the world of juvenile delinquency off the streets and brought it into a prosperous middle-class neighborhood. The film also gave Dean the role with which he is most identified. His Jim Stark is not so much a rebel; he simply does not understand the world around him.

information.contentTitle: Scenes from Rebel Without a Cause (1955)
information.contentText: Actor Frank Mazzola (b. 1935) had been part of a Hollywood street gang and taught James Dean how to fight realistically with a knife.

content_list.content_text: In Blackboard Jungle (1955), Richard Brooks (1912-1992) brings juvenile delinquency back into the inner-city school system. With a touch of well-meaning social criticism, and Glenn Ford as a teacher forced to confront his delinquent students, the film was overshadowed by its inclusion of Bill Haley's song "Rock Around the Clock".

content_list.content_text: It was the first major Hollywood film to use rock music on its soundtrack, and in British cinemas teenagers caused disturbances at screenings of the film. In the 1950s, rock, not cinema, was the ultimate expression of youth experience, with the young Elvis Presley (1935-1977) as its charismatic god.

information.contentText: The scene, considered legendary, in which he performs a dance number in prison to the film's title song, was choreographed by Elvis himself; many consider it one of the first music videos in rock history.

content_list.content_text: Presley's film career began with dramatic roles; Jailhouse Rock (1957) was one of the few films to capture the rawness of his early years. After his Army service, his acting career went into decline, with a string of good-guy roles in increasingly tedious musicals.

Too amorphous to be considered a genre, these 1950s films seem to show that Hollywood was trying to understand and exploit both the new generation and the discontents of youth. James Dean's brief career produced one of the definitive portrayals of America's mid-twentieth-century rebel generation. His death, before the release of Rebel Without a Cause, forever fixed his image as an anguished, lost teenager.

information.contentText: Clare Boothe Luce, then U.S. ambassador to Italy, prevented the film from being shown at the Venice Film Festival. In addition, a Senate committee had decided that the film would have no beneficial effects on young people. But these incidents only served to boost the film's publicity and ticket sales.

content_list.content_text: By the mid-1960s, the emerging counterculture had changed productions aimed at teenagers. In 1966, Roger Corman (b. 1926) directed biker films such as The Wild Angels (1966). Featuring a gang of rapists and a biker's funeral with a coffin draped in a Nazi flag, The Wild Angels is far more confrontational than The Wild One.

movies.title: The Wild One
movies.overview: The Black Rebels Motorcycle Club ride into the small California town of Wrightsville, eager to raise hell. Brooding gang leader Johnny Strabler takes a liking to Kathie, the daughter of the local lawman, as another club rolls into town.

movies.title: Rebel Without a Cause
movies.overview: After moving to a new town, troublemaking teen Jim Stark is supposed to have a clean slate, although being the new kid in town brings its own problems. While searching for some stability, Stark forms a bond with a disturbed classmate, Plato, and falls for local girl Judy. However, Judy is the girlfriend of neighborhood tough, Buzz. When Buzz violently confronts Jim and challenges him to a drag race, the new kid's real troubles begin.

movies.title: Jailhouse Rock
movies.overview: After serving time for manslaughter, young Vince Everett becomes a teenage rock star.

movies.title: Blackboard Jungle
movies.overview: Richard Dadier is a teacher at North Manual High School, an inner-city school where many of the pupils frequently engage in anti-social behavior. Dadier makes various attempts to engage the students' interest in education, challenging both the school staff and the pupils. He is subjected to violence as well as duplicitous schemes.

movies.title: Easy Rider
movies.overview: A cross-country trip to sell drugs puts two hippie bikers on a collision course with small-town prejudices.

movies.title: East of Eden
movies.overview: In the Salinas Valley, in and around World War I, Cal Trask feels he must compete against overwhelming odds with his brother for the love of their father. Cal is frustrated at every turn, from his reaction to the war, to how to get ahead in business and in life, to how to relate to estranged mother.

content_list.description: Asian cinema gains even more prominence with the release of several masterpieces. Film noir emerges and musicals continue to shine on the big screen. The Western holds on to its reign as one of the most popular genres, and one of the most important movements in cinema takes place in France: the French New Wave.
